title: Load settings that may have no value

blocks.text: Each service reads its settings from a configuration file, and a parser turns the file into a map from key to value. `Settings` keeps what the admin page shows:

Operators often leave a key in the file with no value, such as `retries:`, to say "use the built-in default", and the parser gives that key the value `null`. Such keys belong in `unset()`, not in `values()`. Any other type means the file is wrong, and the load must stop with an `IllegalArgumentException` that names the key: last quarter a `ratio: 0.75` went unnoticed for a week because the service treated it as missing.
Write `put(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/Settings.java`. About seven lines in total.

cases.says: strings, integers, booleans and lists are stored as the text the admin page shows
a key the file names without a value is listed as unset, and loading goes on
a value of a type the settings don't support stops the load with an IllegalArgumentException naming its key, rather than being listed as unset

origin.section: null Matches Only case null; Neither default Nor case Object Does

concepts: case null, default sends null and every unhandled type to one arm, so it fits only where missing and unsupported mean the same thing.
A null selector matches only case null; without it the switch throws NullPointerException before any case, even with a default or a case Object o.
